detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Make `cfg.model` and `cfg.model.transformer` authoritative for shared model construction and training-loop consumers (C10 of the training-loop consolidation).

- Preserve GPT/Hybrid builders and BERT/T5/VLM/MIMO provider callbacks. Callback paths get a typed model-provider config centrally; position capacity stays distinct from actual data sequence length.
- Read model precision, topology, attention/MoE, recomputation, graph and freeze settings from config in startup, model setup, training/evaluation, warmup, FLOPs and memory estimates. Derive optimizer precision and runtime batch topology centrally. GPT/Hybrid embedding groups, batch layouts and sampler/collation selection use the same model owner.
- Restore model settings from existing checkpoint config metadata, retaining legacy checkpoint fallback and existing CLI override rules. Preserve nested Hybrid/MTP specs and activation settings through serialization.
- Keep TP user-buffer overrides on the existing model owners, with explicit actual sequence length and microbatch inputs. No new overlap config.
- Pass model-owned TP/divisibility inputs explicitly to tokenizer padding during training bootstrap; preserve explicit padded-vocabulary overrides and existing inference defaults. Tokenizer selection and policy remain separate.

Upcycling policy/native-builder changes remain a follow-up; existing callback upcycling is preserved. `modelopt_enabled` remains with the distillation integration (C17). Tokenizer, optimizer and scheduler ownership migrations are separate.

This is an independent draft on main. Integration with #7778, #8149, #8205 and #8202 must retain their distributed/training/DDP owners and centralized finalization contracts; this PR does not replace those migrations.

## Why keep this migration in one PR?

We considered splitting this PR, but the model-config ownership switch needs to be atomic: initialization, model construction, training consumers, and checkpoint handling must agree on the source of truth. Splitting those would leave some paths reading `args` and others reading `cfg.model`, or require temporary compatibility code.

The current 102-file diff includes 51 test files, 23 of which change by at most 12 lines. Serialization could be extracted independently, but that would only reduce this PR to roughly 95 files. Keeping these changes together lets reviewers verify the complete ownership change and its tests in one place.

## Issue tracking

Related to #3554.

## Validation

Targeted existing unit modules on eight GPUs: **1,150 passed, 116 skipped per rank**, at `18fc331bf5ea10730268186c0ddee9ef59b08318`. Covers model builders/serialization, callback/MIMO boundaries, startup, checkpoint/resume, RNG, warmup, FLOPs/memory, logging, batch layouts and sampler/collation behavior. The skips are 113 layouts requiring more than eight GPUs and three GTP checks requiring Transformer Engine >=2.19. Includes divergent config/CLI inputs for model topology and vocabulary padding. Independent complete-diff and follow-up review are complete. This is not a full unit or functional-suite claim. No GPU kernel algorithm changes or new golden values.

All-files pre-commit reproduces existing Black/Pylint failures outside this change; isort passes. No unrelated formatting changes were included.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests (existing test modules, including callback and checkpoint behavior)
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel, I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test (not applicable: configuration/API refactor)
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [x] I have added relevant documentation (configuration fields and API docstrings)
- [ ] I have run the autoformatter on my PR (local wrapper requires Git >=2.31; scoped checks and all-files pre-commit run separately)

### Code review

Keep this PR in draft while integration and CI review proceed.

[P2] Preserve deferred vocabulary resolution in dynamic-server startup

**Failure:** With valid model dimensions, padding enabled, and no explicit padded vocabulary—for example an args-free checkpoint whose architecture and HF tokenizer are supplied on the CLI—this new fallback constructs a model config even though `build_model_config=False`. Its vocabulary remains `None`. The [dynamic server](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/tools/run_dynamic_text_generation_server.py#L172-L191) intentionally calls `initialize_megatron(build_tokenizer=False)` before checkpoint-family detection and tokenizer rebuilding. However, [runtime initialization](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/training/global_vars.py#L191-L200) still invokes the [vocabulary resolver](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/training/argument_utils.py#L590-L595), which raises `Model vocabulary must be resolved before model construction`. Startup never reaches the tokenizer that would resolve it. The [base implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/d5cc5e6d816a037a3b5ca97848ed81e852a66b89/megatron/training/argument_utils.py#L856-L863) honored the explicit deferral.

**Correction:** Coordinate this factory with `parse_args_and_detect_vlm()` and runtime vocabulary binding so this explicitly deferred bootstrap can finish before vocabulary resolution is required. Construct or refresh the final model config after detection and bind the rebuilt tokenizer before model construction. Simply restoring `model=None` without updating the text-only path is incomplete because the migrated `get_model()` now needs `cfg.model.transformer`. The exact deferral API is an implementation choice; the invariant is that initialization without tokenization must not require a tokenizer-derived vocabulary prematurely, while actual model construction must require a resolved one.

**Preservation:** Keep eager validation for ordinary non-deferred startup, explicit padded-vocabulary precedence, normal GPT/Hybrid configuration selection, ordinary LLaVA selection, and the MIMO prefix-map/provider specialization rather than replacing every VLM with the ordinary LLaVA callback.

**Proposed acceptance checks:** Exercise the server bootstrap with model dimensions present, `pad_vocab_size=True`, `padded_vocab_size=None`, and a mocked tokenizer vocabulary of 261. Both text-only and args-free VLM detection must reach tokenizer rebuilding and obtain the correctly padded model vocabulary before construction. Retain explicit padded-size overrides and MIMO prefix-map dispatch. A non-deferred model-construction attempt with unresolved vocabulary must still raise the existing error. These checks were not executed.

inline_comments.body:
Compared #8234 at `ea54f674` with #8341 at `f8807e82c`. I'd favor #8341's `GTPParallelLayout` calculation combined with this PR's model-world-size resolution.

For valid inputs and the same world size, both calculate:

```python
configured_cp = transformer.context_parallel_size // sequence_shards
dp = world_size // (tp * pp * configured_cp * weight_size)
```

Both correctly divide out the GTP sequence shards already included in the transformer's resolved CP. `GTPParallelLayout` centralizes the arithmetic and validation and also exposes `batch_parallel_size`, which this PR calculates separately. Constructing it only validates integers; it does not initialize process groups or enumerate ranks.

The implementations differ on invalid inputs: the layout checks that sequence shards divide the weight-remat size, whereas this PR's method does not. Conversely, #8341's `getattr(..., 1) or 1` silently converts zero shard/weight sizes to one; I would avoid that normalization for fields that should already be valid.

For world-size handling, the explicit argument in #8341 makes the calculation deterministic and convenient for tests or hypothetical launch sizes. This PR's no-argument API is convenient for runtime callers, but `get_model_world_size()` also provides an important semantic distinction: MIMO's model world size can be smaller than the global launch. It selects `mimo_llm_world_size` when configured and checks that it fits within the launch. #8341 currently passes `safe_get_world_size()` directly, without that model-subset handling.

My preference would be a shared layout-construction method taking an explicit **model world size**, with runtime callers obtaining that value through `get_model_world_size()`. A no-argument convenience method can wrap those steps. This keeps environment discovery at the runtime boundary while centralizing topology calculations and retaining MIMO handling.

Sources: [#8234 implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ea54f6741308799cd83fa961aa61a675f059f195/megatron/training/config/container.py#L247-L289), [#8341 implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f8807e82c144949f18416dfee6be1922920ef129/megatron/training/config/container.py#L424-L450).


Concretely, keeping this PR's `get_model_world_size()` and omitting layout arguments/validation for brevity:

```python
def get_parallel_layout(self, model_world_size: int) -> GTPParallelLayout:
    # Validate and translate the model config into layout inputs.
    return GTPParallelLayout(...)


def get_data_parallel_size(self) -> int:
    return self.get_parallel_layout(self.get_model_world_size()).dp


def get_batch_parallel_size(self) -> int:
    return self.get_parallel_layout(self.get_model_world_size()).batch_parallel_size
```

### Code review

Found 2 additional issues:

1. **[P2] Update converter model config after vocabulary repadding.** `initialize_megatron_env()` now captures the source checkpoint's padded vocabulary in `cfg.model`, but `receive_lm()` subsequently updates only `self.margs.padded_vocab_size` for the target TP size. The migrated BERT provider reads `cfg.model`, so converting a vocabulary of 30,522 tokens from TP=1 to TP=8 builds embedding shards with 3,824 rows while the repadded incoming shards have 3,840 rows. The embedding copy then fails. Please synchronize the model/tokenizer vocabulary config after target padding is resolved and before constructing models or saving metadata. (bug)

https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/8999d2a86c888f1929dea95f0e16239f32356af7/tools/checkpoint/saver_base.py#L160-L164

#### Cross-repo impact (Megatron-Bridge)

2. **[P2] Preserve subclass conversion hooks in the shared serializer.** Calling `serialize_dataclass(self)` bypasses Bridge's `_convert_value_to_dict()` override, including recursive conversions. For example, Bridge converts `PipelineParallelLayerLayout` back to its constructor input; without that hook, YAML falls back to a class target without the required layout/parallel-size arguments, so the saved config cannot be reconstructed. The override also handles HF configs and GTP shard settings. Please retain recursive customization or coordinate the Bridge migration before changing this contract. (breakage)

Found three P2 issues: one inline and two below. This was a static review; tests were not executed. Checkpoint/serialization coverage was completed directly after one delegated report was unavailable. The converter vocabulary-repadding fix is present and has regression assertions for expansion, shrinking, and unchanged sizes.

### [P2] Recursively encode explicit BERT specs before YAML serialization

**Failure:** Set `BertModelConfig.transformer_layer_spec` to `bert_layer_local_spec`, save the containing run config with `to_yaml()`, then reload it with `from_yaml()`. The new callback config is a plain dataclass, so [the shared serializer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/training/config/utils.py#L25-L58) leaves callable encoding disabled for its spec. The [local BERT spec](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/core/models/bert/bert_layer_specs.py#L82-L112) contains an MLP partial whose `submodules` argument is an `MLPSubmodules` instance. The [YAML partial representer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/training/config/yaml_utils.py#L106-L156) passes that instance through to the generic object representer, which records its class but loses its fields. Reloading consequently attempts `MLPSubmodules()` without the [required `linear_fc1` and `linear_fc2` arguments](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/core/transformer/mlp.py#L140-L151). The saved configuration should reconstruct the selected spec.

**Correction:** Enable recursive callable encoding for `ModuleSpec` subtrees, without changing ordinary container callable passthrough. A small proposed patch in [config/utils.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/training/config/utils.py#L12-L58) is:

```python
from megatron.core.transformer.spec_utils import ModuleSpec

# In serialize_dataclass(), immediately after the TransformerConfig branch:
if isinstance(config, ModuleSpec):
    encode_callables = True
```

This sends the nested partial through the existing `_encode_callable()` implementation, which recursively serializes its dataclass arguments. Please verify the suggestion before adopting it.

**Preservation and proposed acceptance checks:** Extend [the BERT boundary test](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/tests/unit_tests/training/test_initialization_lifecycle.py#L625-L644) with an actual YAML round trip for local and custom `ModuleSpec` inputs. Assert that the restored MLP partial retains its function and both linear builders. Retain the `None` case selecting the default TE spec, ordinary container callable identity assertions in [test_container_base.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/tests/unit_tests/training/config/test_container_base.py#L776-L790), and the Hybrid nested MTP/MLP spec assertions in [test_base.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/tests/unit_tests/training/models/test_base.py#L386-L424).

### [P2] Expect the config-validation error for a zero-sized MIMO grid

**Failure:** The `(world_size=4, mimo_llm_world_size=0)` case in [test_training_topology_rejects_invalid_rank_counts](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/tests/unit_tests/training/test_initialization_lifecycle.py#L1035-L1053) deterministically fails its regex assertion. `finalize()` [calls `validate()` first](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/training/config/container.py#L81-L85), and [config-only validation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/0c73f01ba6897ec06fbb16294d12e696e2836ee8/megatron/training/config/container.py#L414-L420) correctly raises `MIMO language-model world size must be positive`, not the universally expected `Training model world size must fit`.

**Correction:** Change only this test's expected message; retain the early production validation. Replace the `pytest.raises` block at lines 1050–1051 with:

```python
expected_error = (
    "MIMO language-model world size must be positive"
    if mimo_llm_world_size == 0
    else "Training model world size must fit"
)
with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=expected_error):
    run_config.finalize()
```

**Preservation and proposed acceptance checks:** All four parameter cases must pass: zero/negative launch sizes and a model grid larger than the launch still expect the runtime fit error; the zero-sized MIMO grid expects the config-only positivity error. Keep the assertions that rejection leaves the serialized config unchanged and `_finalized` false. Config-only validation must continue rejecting nonpositive MIMO sizes without querying launch state.
